objective: Make Crowley's current and future durable state safely evolvable, inspectable, backed up, and recoverable before adding sessions, Spaces, personal operations, Forge runs, or connectors.
context: Approved plan: docs/V4.3.3R_RECOVERY_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md. North star: docs/V5_LIFE_READY_COGNITIVE_OS_PLAN.md. Baseline main commit ab04924189cde80cb80b341fcbf3256b236497c3 locks V4.3.1-V4.3.2. A current crowley.db exists but its provenance and historical lock-document counts are not assumed. The Windows bridge, encrypted backup work, and repaired Python 3.12 environment are checkpointed inputs that must be reviewed rather than treated as recovery-lock proof. Historical V4.3.3 tickets #491-#495 are absent from the current reset database; their do-not-claim/superseded status must be preserved in repository documentation and a current Crowley receipt without fabricating ticket events.
decisions: Adopt and preserve compatible existing databases; do not presume a clean reset.
Use an ordered migration ledger with explicit empty-database and audited legacy-adoption paths.

Treat migration, core compatibility schema, memory compatibility, write audit, observability, and Sparks as required startup subsystems; optional embeddings and external providers may degrade visibly.
Enable foreign-key enforcement on every application connection after orphan preflight; add constraints progressively instead of rebuilding every legacy table in this release.
Retain the compatibility Crowley project and defer canonical Space creation until the project-versus-Space decision.
Keep memory_items as mixed compatibility state for now; new cognitive behavior remains Spark-first and V4.4 owns final chat fallback tiering.
A backup is verified only after isolated restore, integrity checks, migrations, required startup health, and bounded application smoke.
Preserve crowley.py as an import-compatible facade and keep new migration/recovery logic in focused modules.
non_goals: Deleting, draining, bulk-archiving, or reconstructing current database rows
Replaying historical artifacts as fabricated live events
Creating Spaces, conversation sessions, personal operations, agent runs, durable jobs, MCP, connectors, or voice
Rebuilding every legacy table solely to add foreign keys
Removing existing public APIs, Actions shapes, or crowley.py compatibility
Automatically replacing the live database during restore
Storing the only backup recovery key with the database, repository, or encrypted backup
risks: The current database may contain an unknown or incompatible schema and must be preserved before adoption.
Enabling foreign keys may expose existing orphaned references or tests that relied on unenforced relationships.
Python environment repair and external restic/R2 configuration are operational dependencies, not proof of repository correctness.
SQLite migration transaction behavior and concurrent startup require explicit failure and locking tests.
The checkpointed recovery implementation overlaps this ladder and must not be overwritten or treated as recovery-lock proof.
Backup success can create false confidence unless application-aware restore verification is mandatory.
qa_expectations: Each slice runs its focused tests. Schema-changing slices test empty, compatible existing, incompatible, repeated, interrupted, and concurrent behavior. Recovery slices test tamper, missing-key, isolated restore, and live-state preservation. The final lock requires full unittest discovery, preflight, clean-bootstrap acceptance, existing-database adoption, and bounded restored-copy API/cognitive smoke. Verification must use isolated databases and never mutate the live crowley.db.
next_action: Post the approved do-not-claim notice for historical V4.3.3 tickets #491-#495, preserve that the rows are absent from the current reset database, then mint this seven-ticket ladder and activate only R1.

approval.note: The V5 and V4.3.3R plans and this concrete seven-ticket packet were approved by Mr. Go on 2026-07-28. The Python runtime was repaired and verified. Before minting, preserve a do-not-claim notice for historical V4.3.3 tickets #491-#495; because those rows are absent from the current reset database, do not fabricate cancellation events.

tickets.title: V4.3.3R R1: runtime preflight and current-state preservation
tickets.description: Establish an executable, reproducible Crowley environment and preserve current durable state before schema work. Convert the verified local Python 3.12 repair into repository-supported setup and preflight without embedding machine-specific paths. Perform metadata-only database inspection (file identity, integrity, schema fingerprint, migration/user version, table names/counts; no row-content export), create and verify a pre-change online snapshot, and write a provenance status artifact. Review the checkpointed Windows bridge/backup implementation without overwriting it or treating it as recovery-lock proof. Likely surfaces: requirements files, setup/operator docs, a focused preflight or schema-inspection script, existing scripts/crowley_backup.py, and isolated tests. Depends on the approved V4.3.3R plan.
tickets.non_goals: Schema mutation; database reset; corpus drain; installing or configuring external R2 credentials as test truth; committing secrets.
tickets.qa_expectation: Focused environment/preflight and snapshot tests; metadata inspection against an isolated fixture and the current DB in read-only mode; prove no live rows change.
acceptance: Repository instructions produce a working Python environment without relying on the removed Python311 path
Current crowley.db is inspected read-only and receives a provenance status without exporting row contents
A consistent pre-change snapshot is created and passes checksum plus SQLite integrity verification
Checkpointed recovery and Windows bridge work is preserved and explicitly inventoried
No schema or live database row is changed by R1
Focused tests and exact verification commands are recorded in the handoff

tickets.title: V4.3.3R R2: schema inventory and migration contract lock
tickets.description: Produce the reviewed schema inventory and implementation contract before migration code. Inventory every table, index, trigger, declared foreign key, runtime ALTER/column check, direct sqlite3 opener, setup owner, and required/optional subsystem across crowley.py and focused modules. Lock migration ledger fields, checksum semantics, empty-database creation, existing-database baseline adoption, transaction/locking rules, schema fingerprinting, incompatibility behavior, and compatibility implications for APIs, tools, tests, scripts, and backup. Add docs/V4.3.3R_MIGRATION_CONTRACT.md plus deterministic inventory tooling/artifact if useful. Depends on R1.
tickets.non_goals: Implementing the migration runner; modifying schema; rebuilding legacy tables; changing APIs.
tickets.qa_expectation: Inventory test or deterministic comparison proves all committed schema creators and runtime column additions are represented; Codex architecture review before R3.
acceptance: Inventory covers every committed CREATE TABLE, index, trigger, ALTER/add-column path, and direct database connection
Required and optional startup subsystems are explicitly classified
Migration identity, checksum, transaction, locking, adoption, and failure contracts are unambiguous
Compatibility effects on setup_db, tests, APIs, Actions, scripts, backup, and Spark foreign keys are recorded
No migration implementation or database mutation lands in R2
Codex approves the migration contract before R3 may begin

tickets.title: V4.3.3R R3: ordered migration runner and baseline adoption
tickets.description: Implement a focused migration module and schema_migrations ledger from the approved R2 contract. Support ordered empty-database creation and audited adoption of compatible existing databases without claiming historical migrations ran. Integrate through a thin crowley.setup_db compatibility wrapper and the shared test DB helper. Enforce migration IDs/checksums, repeat-safe behavior, bounded migration locking, incompatible-schema rejection, and truthful failure reporting. Preserve all existing public behavior and rows unless the approved baseline migration explicitly requires otherwise. Depends on R2 Codex approval.
tickets.non_goals: Strict startup subsystem registry (R4); foreign-key rollout (R4); domain schema for sessions/Spaces/operations; legacy row deletion.
tickets.qa_expectation: Focused migration tests cover empty, compatible legacy, incompatible, repeat, checksum mismatch, interruption, and concurrent startup fixtures; existing isolated DB tests remain compatible.
acceptance: Empty and adopted-compatible database fixtures reach the same required schema fingerprint
Existing-database adoption is recorded explicitly and does not fabricate historical migration execution
Repeated migration is a no-op and an applied checksum mismatch fails loudly
Incompatible or unknown schema blocks healthy startup without overwriting the database
Interrupted and concurrent migration tests produce one truthful migration owner and recoverable committed state
crowley.setup_db remains an import-compatible wrapper and focused migration tests pass

tickets.title: V4.3.3R R4: strict startup and SQLite integrity enforcement
tickets.description: Replace broad required-initialization exception suppression with an explicit required/optional subsystem registry. Require migration/core schema, memory compatibility, write audit, observability, and Sparks; expose optional embedding/model/tunnel degradation separately. Enable PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON on every shared application connection after adoption orphan preflight. Add foreign_key_check/orphan reporting, schema/startup health fields, and focused failure injection. Keep business logic out of app.py and new feature logic out of crowley.py. Depends on R3.
tickets.non_goals: Rebuilding every legacy table; making external providers required; changing domain APIs beyond approved additive health fields.
tickets.qa_expectation: Connection pragma, required failure, optional degradation, orphan preflight, health redaction, and existing Spark foreign-key behavior tests.
acceptance: Every normal application connection has foreign_keys enabled and retains WAL/busy-timeout behavior
Required subsystem failure prevents healthy startup and identifies the failing subsystem
Optional provider or embedding failure reports degraded status without hiding the reason
Existing orphaned references block adoption or produce an explicit repair requirement and are never silently deleted
Health output exposes migration/schema and subsystem status without secrets
Focused startup/integrity tests and relevant existing database tests pass

tickets.title: V4.3.3R R5: versioned recovery bundle and key contract
tickets.description: Review and integrate the checkpointed encrypted recovery implementation under a stable, versioned bundle contract. Expand the manifest to classify all durable artifacts and excluded configuration, include migration version/schema fingerprint/tool format/rebuild metadata, checksum included artifacts, preserve online SQLite snapshot consistency, and keep recovery keys outside ordinary backup contents. Support isolated local restic integration tests plus the documented encrypted off-device operator path. Surface backup freshness and last verification without claiming upload equals recovery. Likely surfaces: scripts/crowley_backup.py, tests/test_crowley_backup.py, docs/DISASTER_RECOVERY.md, health/preflight adapters. Depends on R3 and coordinates with R4 health.
tickets.non_goals: Uploading test data to a real cloud account; committing credentials; automatic live restore; field-level Spark encryption; connector framework.
tickets.qa_expectation: Snapshot consistency, complete manifest classification, checksum/tamper, DPAPI where available, local restic integration, secret redaction, and live-path isolation tests.
acceptance: Recovery manifest is versioned and records migration version, schema fingerprint, repository state, artifact checksums, exclusions, and rebuild metadata
Bundle scope explicitly classifies database, processed/inbox state, brain configuration, managed artifacts, connector/schedule configuration, and secrets
The only recovery key is never stored in Git, the database, the encrypted repository, ordinary logs, manifests, or handoffs
Backup status distinguishes snapshot/upload success from verified restore
Local isolated integration tests do not require real R2 credentials and external operator steps remain documented
Existing user recovery work is preserved, reviewed, and covered by focused tests

tickets.title: V4.3.3R R6: application-aware restore and recovery failure injection
tickets.description: Extend restore verification beyond hashes and SQLite integrity. Restore into an isolated path, verify manifest/artifact checksums, run migrations against the restored copy, initialize required subsystems, and execute bounded health, ticket, Spark, and cognitive-context smoke without touching live state. Add clean-machine-equivalent acceptance tooling and failure injection for corrupt backup, missing key, interrupted migration, partial required initialization, concurrent startup, and stale recovery locks. Record drill reports suitable for health/operations. Depends on R4 and R5.
tickets.non_goals: Automated promotion of restored data to live; destructive restore; full production connector recovery; user-facing recovery UI.
tickets.qa_expectation: Isolated restore integration suite plus failure matrix; verify the live database path and checksum remain unchanged throughout drills.
acceptance: A restored copy passes manifest hashes, SQLite integrity, ordered migrations, and required subsystem startup
Bounded restored-copy health, ticket, Spark, and cognitive-context smoke passes without using live state
Corrupt backup, missing key, interrupted migration, partial initialization, concurrent startup, and stale-lock fixtures fail truthfully
Restore drill records a durable report with snapshot identity and verification results
Automated restore never replaces or mutates live crowley.db
Clean-machine-equivalent acceptance commands are documented and reproducible

Confirm the repository notice and current Crowley receipt preserving the supersession of old V4.3.3 #491-#495, whose rows are absent from the reset database.
